dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: Hmm? Why is a civilian like you wandering around in the military camp?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: You're on the battlefield. For your own safety, you'd best leave now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: I am Kujou Masahito, a Shogunate officer. I've been stationed in Kannazuka with orders to command the troops here.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: Yes, it's the same Kujou that you are thinking of. The head of the Kujou Clan is my father. If you've ever heard of our clan before, then you should know what it means for me to be here.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: Ever since the war with the Sangonomiya resistance began, this place has been rocked by turmoil. It's not a suitable place for travel or adventuring.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: Please heed my advice and leave now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's the war going?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: As you can see, the conflict is endless. We're in a stalemate. To be honest, if this keeps going on, it's hard to say which side has the upper hand.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: While I was thinking about stratagems lately, my mind would often turn to my discussions of government affairs with Kamaji, my younger brother, about whether the policies in Inazuma are really correct or not...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: Ah, forget it. There is no use in talking about this. And these matters are none of your concern, anyway. A commoner is better off staying far away from the battlefield.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: Hmm? Why is a civilian like you wandering around in the military camp?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: ...Wait, I think I know you, Traveler. Kamaji and Sara have both mentioned you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's things with your little brother?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: My brother Kamaji is currently serving as the Provisional Clan Head in Inazuma City. Being a military man first and foremost, I will support him as best I can.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: Now that our clan is in crisis, there will be those who may have a change of heart, never mind how the Almighty Shogun has yet to pass final judgment upon us. There is still much to be concerned about.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: I've heard that it was you who accompanied the Shogun to rescue my brother from the hands of the Takatsukasa Clan. I, Masahito, will not forget this favor.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: His faith in restoring our clan seems to have been renewed after that incident as well. I, too, believe that there is hope.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Kujou Sara...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: She mentioned that both you and Sangonomiya Kokomi showed up at the signing of the ceasefire, and that you were one of the witnesses to the peace talks.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: I will be honest. While I do not disagree with the results of the peace talks themselves, I am under no illusions that the differences between the Shogunate and the Sangonomiya will be wiped away so easily.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: We of the Shogunate serve the Almighty Shogun, while Sangonomiya worships the already-slain god, Orobaxi. Such a huge gulf in our beliefs will not be bridged by a little ceasefire agreement.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: As an officer of the Shogun's army, I will not relax my vigil simply because of this brief peace.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: As for you... If you were to be on the other side when conflict breaks out again, I will have to face you in battle.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: Mm, be on your way then. This is not some place you'd want to stay in for long.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Tatarigami...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: If we were able to gain more an upper hand during the war, we could have used this matter as a bargaining chip.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: But since the peace talks are over, there's no point considering that what-if now.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: I must say that Sangonomiya Kokomi really is quite impressive...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: If a such a great disaster happened under another leader's watch, it would surely have hurt their image and restrained their next steps...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: But she rooted out the people who performed the inside job and punished them swiftly and severely. If anything, this whole disaster became a way for her to consolidate her position.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: Considering that we were up against such a frightening foe... All the more do I not regret negotiating a peaceful settlement.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, how's the situation on Yashiori Island now?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: We've begun reconstruction and redevelopment efforts in cooperation with Sangonomiya. This will, of course, damage our imports of Jade Steel, but there's nothing to be done.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: After all, we've ignored their humiliation for so long as we exploited an entity that they considered divine...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: I'm sorry. I'm afraid this as far as I can go without speaking out of turn.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: Whatever the case, the things that happened during the war did not surprise me at all. Were my father at the head of our troops, I suspect that his methods would have been crueler still...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Masahito
dialogues.text: Indeed, he would probably see it as what ought to be done.
